newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX TRADE PENA TO HOUSTON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX TRADE PENA TO HOUSTON.

text.p: The Chicago White Sox traded veteran catcher Tony Pena to the Houston Astros Thursday for minor-league pitcher Julien Tucker.
pena, 40, batted .164 (11-for-67) with no homers and eight RBI in 31 games for the White Sox this season. He ranks fourth on baseball's all-time games caught list with 1,942.

"We really appreciate Tony and the role he played with some of our young pitchers," said Chicago general manager Ron Scheuler. "But we are pleased to acquire another young pitcher with a quality arm for our system."

In his five-year career in the Astros organization, Tucker, a native Canadian, was 24-32 with a 4.08 ERA. The right-hander had a 8-7 mark and a 5.22 ERA this season at Class-A Kissimmee of the Florida State League. The 24-year old will report to Class-A Hickory, Chicago's affiliate in the South Atlantic League.
Pena's games played as a catcher trails only Carlton Fisk (2,226), Bob Boone (2,225), and Gary Carter (2,056). Fisk will have his number 72 retired by the White Sox on September 14th.
